meta.title: A teaching edition of Query-Dependent Weighted Memory
meta.subtitle: From fixed averaging to a query-dependent weighted readout

learning_outcomes.description: Explain why uniform averaging cannot respond to a changed query when stored values stay fixed.
Distinguish the roles of query, keys, scores, weights, and values.
Calculate a small weighted sum and identify the equal-score case as the ordinary mean.
Trace which quantities can change when the query, keys, or values change.
Separate algebraic consequences from unsupported empirical claims.

sections.title: Before the paper: vectors and weighted sums
sections.paper_explanation: This teaching section supplies mathematical background rather than reporting a section of the fictional paper. A weighted sum gives each value a coefficient before adding the contributions.
sections.simple_explanation: Separate deciding how much each record contributes from combining its contents. Equal coefficients produce an ordinary average.

intuition.explanation: A weighted average preserves averaging while allowing unequal shares.

boundaries.description: The small examples introduce the arithmetic; paper value rows may contain several coordinates.

sections.title: The paper's question: can a memory read depend on the request?
sections.paper_explanation: The paper considers paired keys and values and asks for a transparent rule whose output can depend on a supplied query.
sections.simple_explanation: The same collection can be read differently for different requests because matching information is separated from returned content.

intuition.explanation: Imagine notes with labels and contents: compare a request with labels, then combine contents.

boundaries.description: The query, keys, and values are supplied inputs; their learning is outside the paper.

sections.title: The problem with always taking the same mean
sections.paper_explanation: The baseline adds stored values and divides by their count. Its equal coefficients contain no query-dependent term.
sections.simple_explanation: The mean is not wrong; it answers a fixed question rather than one whose coefficients depend on the request.

boundaries.description: Uniform averaging remains suitable when equal contributions are intended.

sections.title: The proposed solution: compare, normalize, combine
sections.paper_explanation: Scaled query-key dot products produce scores, softmax turns scores into coefficients, and those coefficients combine the corresponding values.
sections.simple_explanation: Keys are used for comparison and values supply content. The calculation keeps those two roles distinct.

equations.explanation: Compare the query with each key using the source's scale.
Convert scores into positive coefficients that sum to one.
Use the coefficients to combine the value rows.

guided_explorations.title: Change the query
guided_explorations.instruction: Change the query entries while leaving keys and values fixed.
guided_explorations.observe: Watch which score and coefficient changes.
guided_explorations.explanation: The query participates in matching and can therefore alter the coefficients.

guided_explorations.title: Change only the values
guided_explorations.instruction: Edit the value rows without changing the query or keys.
guided_explorations.observe: The coefficients stay fixed while the readout changes.
guided_explorations.explanation: Values enter only the final weighted combination in this model.

boundaries.description: Query width equals key-row width, and key and value row counts match.
The definition uses one query and has no masking, learned projection, or multiple heads.

sections.title: What the equations establish
sections.paper_explanation: Equal scores give coefficients of 1/n, while changing values alone leaves the coefficients unchanged.
sections.simple_explanation: Equal scores mean equal shares. Matching determines shares before values are combined.

intuition.explanation: Read the formula as a dependency chain from scores to coefficients to readout.

boundaries.description: These observations are algebraic consequences, not empirical results.

sections.title: What the paper does not establish
sections.paper_explanation: The paper provides no dataset, benchmark, learned parameters, or empirical comparison.
sections.simple_explanation: The calculation can be checked without pretending that a real application has been validated.

boundaries.description: No empirical evaluation is available in the source.
The coefficients are not a complete explanation of a larger system's decisions.

sections.title: The conclusion: a defined mechanism and an open application question
sections.paper_explanation: The paper replaces fixed equal coefficients with coefficients computed from query-key scores while leaving empirical usefulness unresolved.
sections.simple_explanation: The mechanism has inspectable mathematical properties, but usefulness still requires evidence.

boundaries.description: Whether the reader is useful for an application remains open.

concepts.name: Weighted-sum background
concepts.summary: Coefficients set each value's arithmetic contribution.

concepts.name: Query-dependent memory reading
concepts.summary: The paper asks for a readout that can change with the current request.

concepts.name: Uniform averaging baseline
concepts.summary: Fixed equal coefficients ignore the query.

concepts.name: Query-key matching
concepts.summary: Scaled dot products produce compatibility scores.

concepts.name: Normalized coefficients
concepts.summary: Softmax turns scores into shares summing to one.

concepts.name: Weighted value readout
concepts.summary: Coefficients combine value rows into an output.

concepts.name: Matching and content have separate roles
concepts.summary: Changing values alone leaves the coefficients unchanged.

concepts.summary: Mathematical properties do not establish usefulness.

assessment.prompt: What happens when every compatibility score is equal?
options: The largest value receives all weight
assessment.explanation: Equal softmax numerators produce equal shares whose total is one.

assessment.prompt: If only the value rows change, what remains fixed?
assessment.explanation: The query and keys determine scores and coefficients before values enter the calculation.

assessment.prompt: What additional evidence would be needed to claim that this reader improves an application?
assessment.correct_answer: A task-specific empirical comparison using data and an appropriate baseline.
assessment.explanation: The source establishes algebraic properties but supplies no benchmark evidence.
